reading.text:
Reading (locked before any Lean is shown) — def LevyStochCalc.Probability.predictableSigma

Paper notion (eq:fubiniiso): "P := predictable σ-field on Ω × [0,T]", the σ-algebra
generated by the predictable rectangles (s, t] × F, F ∈ F_s, and {0} × F, F ∈ F_0
(equivalently by left-continuous adapted processes). Faithful Lean definition: the
σ-algebra on time × Ω generated by these sets (for the given filtration). Edge cases:
omitting {0} × F_0 makes predictable processes deterministic at time 0 (only {0} × Ω and ∅
at time 0) — narrower pointwise, harmless up to the dt⊗dP-null set {0} × Ω (the paper's
predictable integrands are equivalence classes, and every identity is dt⊗dP-a.e. or
integrated); using [s, t) or [s, t] would give a non-predictable σ-algebra (defect). Mathlib
has `MeasureTheory.Filtration.predictable`? (if used, check its generators: Mathlib defines
`measurableSpace` predictable via {0}×F_0 sets and (s,t]×F_s sets.)

comparison.text:
Comparison — predictableSigma (LevyStochCalc/Probability/Predictable.lean:28-35)

Lean: generateFrom ({(−∞,0] × A : A ∈ ℱ_0} ∪ {(r,∞) × A : r ∈ ℝ, A ∈ ℱ_r}) on ℝ × Ω.
Against my reading (σ generated by (s,t] × F, F ∈ F_s, and {0} × F, F ∈ F_0):
- Trace on [0,∞) × Ω: {0} × A (A ∈ ℱ_0) from the initial cell; (r,t] × A = (r,∞) × A ∖ (t,∞) × A
  for r ≥ 0; (r,∞) × A = ⋃_n (r, r+n] × A; for r < 0, [0,∞) × A = {0} × A ∪ (0,∞) × A with
  A ∈ ℱ_r ⊆ ℱ_0. So it equals the classical predictable σ-algebra on [0,∞) × Ω, initial cell
  included (the time-0 edge case I flagged does not occur here).
- Left-open intervals with the event known at the left end: the predictable (not optional)
  form.
- On negative times extra structure from ℱ_r (r < 0) and all of B(ℝ) × Ω via (r,∞) × Ω: absent
  from the paper; processes extended by 0 are measurable for it. Mathlib's
  Filtration.predictable needs an index with ⊥; the docstring of the file says this replaces the
  bottom cell by (−∞,0] × A under the convention that ℱ is constant on (−∞,0].
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices of predictableSigma, and why each is harmless:
1. Index ℝ with initial cell (−∞,0] × A (A ∈ ℱ_0) and half-lines (r,∞) × A (A ∈ ℱ_r): on
   [0,∞) × Ω the generated σ-algebra is exactly the classical predictable σ-algebra (shown by
   differences and countable unions of generators), so the paper's predictable processes,
   extended by 0 to negative times, are measurable for it and conversely.
2. Negative times carry extra (irrelevant) structure; the paper has no negative times.
